title: Utility Relations Consultant – Large Load Development – Montana
description:
About the role

Alpha Digital One is a private developer of large-load commercial and industrial projects. We are looking for a consultant with electric utility or cooperative experience to support early-stage site research and utility outreach in Montana.

What you will do

* Research electric service territories and infrastructure in Montana.
* Contact cooperatives and utilities to understand their process for serving new large loads.
* Use your industry knowledge to identify the right contacts and open conversations.
* Provide short weekly written updates.

Who we are looking for

* Experience with a Montana electric utility or cooperative — for example NorthWestern Energy, Montana-Dakota Utilities, or one of Montana’s rural electric cooperatives.
* Background in engineering, system planning, staking, key accounts, member services, or economic development.
* Strong local industry relationships.
* Self-directed, clear communicator.
* Former and retired utility professionals are welcome.

Earning potential with completed projects: $150,000–$300,000+ per year. Bonuses are tied to completed projects and are not guaranteed; without a completed project, earnings are the hourly base only.

Please note

* This is an independent contractor engagement. You set your own schedule and methods.
* This role is not open to current employees of an electric utility or cooperative.
* Further project details are shared after an initial conversation and a confidentiality agreement.

To apply, please answer:

1. Which utility or cooperative did you work for, in what role, and during which years?

2. How many hours per week can you commit?

Pay: $28.00 - $34.00 per hour

Expected hours: 10.0 – 40.0 per week

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Application Question(s):

* Do you currently live in Montana?

Experience:

* electric utility or electric cooperative: 1 year (Required)

Work Location: Remote

title: Senior Mechanical Project Engineer
description:
Pacifico Energy develops, finances, builds, and operates energy infrastructure that powers businesses and communities. In the U.S., we are tackling one of the biggest challenges facing AI and large-scale data centers: access to reliable power. Our private grids bring dedicated generation and energy storage directly to customers, helping projects move forward without waiting for traditional utility connections. We draw on Pacifico Energy Group’s experience across the U.S., Japan, South Korea, and Vietnam, spanning solar, wind, battery storage, and natural gas. Joining Pacifico means helping turn ambitious energy projects into operating infrastructure, with work that connects directly to the people and businesses building the future of AI.

We are hiring a Senior Mechanical Project Engineer to serve as the owner’s technical authority for all matters related to design, procurement, and construction of multi-unit simple cycle gas turbine power generation facilities with battery energy storage and associated auxiliary systems. The position supports projects across the company’s power generation development and execution portfolio but may become dedicated to a specific project site during the execution phase.

This role provides engineering leadership late-stage project development through procurement, EPC execution, commissioning, and long-term asset operation. The successful candidate will represent the company as the technical interface with equipment OEMs, Owner’s Engineers, EPC contractors, and other internal and external stakeholders, ensuring best-in-class outcomes for owner-developed and owner-operated generation assets.

title: Senior Director, Utility Strategy and Market Design
description:
**The Role**

Following Madison’s groundbreaking Community Infrastructure announcement to develop 1 GW and mobilize up to $2 billion in capital, we are hiring a leader to own MEI’s relationships with utilities, ISOs/RTOs, and state utility regulators. This person will be critical in helping MEI shape the market rules and utility programs that determine whether distributed storage and solar can be interconnected, accredited, and compensated at the massive scale our plan requires.

This person will own MEI’s influence in those proceedings — identifying which rules actually matter to our thesis, deciding where our effort is best spent, and working directly with utilities and commission staff to craft programs that work for the utility, the Digital Infrastructure Partners, the community, and MEI at the same time.

This is a utility- and regulator-facing role, not a legislative one. A separate hire will own policy and government relations — legislative advocacy, executive branch engagement, and trade association strategy. The external counterparts for this role are the utility resource planner, the distribution engineer, the DER program manager, the commission staffer, and the ISO stakeholder committee: the people who design programs and write rules. The two roles will coordinate closely, but the mandate here is technical, program-level, and commercial.

This person will own MEI’s assessment of market and interconnection viability — verifying that the ISO, RTO, and utility will allow us to interconnect and provide capacity in a given location, now or on a known timeline, and building the path to change that where they will not. That assessment directly determines where MEI commits development capital, so the rigor and honesty of this work matters.

This role translates the VP's industrialized delivery strategy into an executable engineering discipline, leading the Electrical, Mechanical, Manufacturing Engineering, and Systems Engineering leads and their teams to produce fabrication-ready designs that meet IREN's cost, schedule, and quality requirements at scale.
  
  
With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

  

* Minimum 10+ years of experience in electrical, mechanical, or structural engineering with demonstrated expertise in DfMA, modular design, or advanced manufacturing applied to large-scale infrastructure.
* Proven track record establishing DfMA standards and leading multidisciplinary engineering teams (electrical, mechanical, structural) through a modular or off-site delivery model.
* Experience with BIM-to-fabrication work
